analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Market regime is confirmed uptrend (SPY +1.6% vs SMA50), which is a broadly supportive backdrop. However, the historical performance data demands humility — a 0.44x profit factor and -4.33 Sortino Ratio indicate losses have been outpacing gains materially. This argues strongly for quality over quantity and raising the bar on new entries.

Existing positions: MCO (+5.86%) is the standout, thesis intact — high-quality ratings/analytics business with a strong moat. AMP (+1.69%) is performing acceptably. LMT (-2.04%) is marginally underwater but defense spending thesis and UPTREND classification remain intact; hold. IDXX (-2.37%) is the concerning position — it shows MIXED/SIDEWAYS trend, -2.5% below SMA50, and -11.4% below SMA200, sitting at only the 8th percentile of its 52-week range. That said, it is well above its 52w low ($526.44 vs current $545.31), still in the screened quality list, and appears to be basing. No stop has been hit. Monitor closely — a close below $526 would break the base and warrant exit regardless of thesis.

NEW SETUP: After screening the 30 candidates, most are either too extended vs SMA50 (IT +28%, CTSH +25.5%, NOW +19.6%, BR +17.3%, ADBE +17.4% — all rejected per rule), too close to earnings (ADBE in 20 days), or lack a compelling enough combination of value + trend + momentum. Capital One (COF) stands out as the clearest asymmetric setup: fwd P/E 8.84x with PEG 0.23 is the best value in the universe, UPTREND with SMA50 slope of +6.7% (strongest among non-extended candidates), 47% of 52w range (not extended, not distressed), and ATR only 2.4% allowing a tight, well-defined stop. One trade only — preserving discipline given our poor historical profit factor.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $212.50 or better; accept fill up to $214 on a mild pullback to the SMA50 area. If market opens above $215, wait for intraday dip before entering.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Capital One's fwd P/E of 8.84x with PEG 0.23 is among the most compelling value metrics in the S&P 500 quality universe. The Discover Financial acquisition (closing drove the 1111% revenue anomaly) is transformational — it significantly expands COF's network scale, reduces interchange costs, and should be meaningfully accretive to earnings over 2026-2027. With fwd EPS ~$24, even a modest re-rating to 10-11x fwd P/E gets us to the $240 target. FCF generation is robust and ROE at 9% is depressed by the integration period — underlying returns are higher. TECHNICAL: Price is in a confirmed UPTREND, sitting just +2.9% above SMA50 (not extended), SMA50 slope of +6.7% is the strongest upward momentum among non-extended candidates, and 47% of 52w range means we are in the middle of the range — not chasing a breakout. ATR of 2.4% allows a clean 2x ATR stop at $202, creating a well-defined risk box. Next earnings 60 days out gives full time for thesis to develop without immediate event risk.
trades.exit_plan: 1) Hard stop at $202.00 — no exceptions. 2) If thesis breaks (credit quality deteriorates sharply, Discover integration disrupted, fwd EPS revised down >10%), exit regardless of price. 3) If price runs to $240 target, reassess — potentially trim half and let the rest ride toward LTCG threshold if within 6 months of holding. 4) Time stop: if flat or negative after 90 days with no clear trend development, exit and redeploy. 5) Trim or exit before October 20 earnings if position is significantly profitable, to avoid thesis-unwind risk from a single report.
